workarounds.note: the H1 breakBefore (parity odd) is restated because a headings object drops it
every back-matter style sets breakBefore itself: without it the glossary, references and index would inherit the chapters’ odd parity and open after blank pages
bodyText.referenceColor is restated in ink, and col() writes each colour’s hex beside its paletteId, because the palette reaches neither the reference colour nor the design slots
the H1 level keeps span: 'page' on the one-column chapter and appendix pages too: a band laid out in the column is clipped at the column’s top edge, 24 mm below the trim
table headers are bold on white between rules: a header filled in ink shows light seams between its cells on the canvas
the PDF asks for an italic Libertinus Serif Display, which Fontsource does not ship; the kit’s fontsourceProvider falls back to the upright
the glossary, references and index are set ragged, and ragged text is never hyphenated; their entries are short enough that the rag stays shallow

the index’s sub-entries open with two en spaces behind a zero-width space, not an em space: Libertinus’s latin file has no em space, which the canvas measures in a fallback font and postext-pdf 1.4.1 sets with no width on a line without bold or italic runs, so those sub-entries printed flush left

the index’s letters carry their space in a 21 pt line instead of a marginTop: under a page-span opener, the first heading of the first column keeps its marginTop while the heading at the top of the second column drops it, so the two columns would start at different heights

the chapter numeral and the appendix letter are set at lineHeight 0.72 so that their line fits their box: design text whose line is taller than its box ignores verticalAlign 'bottom' and is set from the top, overflowing downwards

the appendix is lettered by hand: in 1.4.1 a heading style cannot change its level's numberingTemplate, so the heading is unnumbered, its letter is an attribute and its tables use a type numbered 'A.{n}'; the working tree's '{1:A}' templates and startAt attribute would replace this once released

the index joins a line ending in a hyphen to the next without it, and every hyphen in an index pattern is optional: 1.4.1 flags a justified line broken after a hard hyphen as hyphenated, like a line broken inside a word, so the pen cannot tell 'meta-' + 'analyses' from 'expos-' + 'itory'
